🌱 Basics · Lesson 4 · 2 min read

Generative AI & Chatbots

How chatbots and image generators create brand-new content.

AI that creates

Most of the AI we've met so far sorts or predicts: spam or not spam, cat or dog. Generative AI creates new content — text, images, music, code and even video. Chatbots such as ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude, and image generators that turn a sentence into a picture, are all generative AI.

Predicting the next word

Chatbots run on large language models (LLMs). An LLM was trained on a huge amount of text to do one thing extremely well: predict what comes next. Text is split into small pieces called tokens — whole words or parts of words. Given “The cat sat on the…”, the model calculates a probability for every possible next token, picks one, adds it to the text and repeats — token by token, very fast. Extra training with feedback from people then teaches it to follow instructions and be helpful.

Why chatbots make things up

An LLM doesn't look facts up in a database (unless it's connected to a search tool). It produces text that sounds likely. Usually that text is right, but sometimes the model confidently invents facts, quotes or sources that don't exist. This is called a hallucination. That's why you should always double-check important information — especially for schoolwork.

Did you know? Ask a chatbot for book sources, and it may give you a perfect-looking title and author for a book that was never written.

Using it wisely

Generative AI is great for brainstorming ideas, explaining a hard topic in a new way, practising a language or getting feedback on your writing. It's a bad idea to copy its answers into homework (you don't learn, and it's often against school rules), to trust facts without checking, or to share personal information. Tip: a clear prompt gets better answers — say what you need, give some context and name the format you want.

Key points

  • Generative AI creates new text, images, sound, code and video.
  • Chatbots are built on LLMs that predict the next token, again and again.
  • They can “hallucinate”, so always check important facts.

Check yourself

Why can a chatbot confidently say something false?

Show the answer

Right answer: It generates likely-sounding text and doesn't automatically check facts

An LLM predicts which words are likely to come next. Likely-sounding isn't the same as true, so it can “hallucinate” facts. Always check important information.
